Themes: a language model small enough to see
PresentationContext.VisualContinuity: Every graphic in the series is a CoCo screen: black on green, amber for the one thing that changed, navy for emphasis, uppercase blocky type.

Style.Rendering: Flat, pixel-precise illustration as if drawn by an MC6847 video chip: a 32-by-16 text grid of blocky 8-by-12 pixel glyphs, hard edges, no anti-aliasing, no gradients, no painterly texture. A faint CRT curvature and phosphor glow are allowed at the edges only.

Lighting.Shadows: None; the only dark areas are black ink on the field

Accents: Amber #FAE53D for the one thing that changed
Bar green #8EFF48 for inverse-video text on black
ColorPalette.Treatment: Black on green as the body. Amber marks the single element the viewer should look at; navy marks arrows and labels of emphasis; nothing else is coloured. Never red on green.

Effects: Slight CRT barrel curvature at the frame edges
Soft phosphor bloom around bright areas
Atmosphere.Mood: Plain, exact, a machine showing its work

ContentDescription: A wireframe box drawn in thin black lines on a green CoCo screen, in a simple oblique view, containing about thirty small round points, each with a dashed drop line to the floor of the box. Six of the points are larger and amber, sit close together in one region, and are labelled in blocky uppercase: ACORN, APPLE, ATARI, COMMODORE, SINCLAIR, TANDY. The rest are small black points spread through another region, unlabelled, with three or four black points high up on their own. Along the bottom of the screen, one caption line in uppercase: TOKENS THAT ARE FOLLOWED BY THE SAME KIND OF TOKEN END UP NEAR EACH OTHER.
CompositionNotes: The words to render, and only these: the six maker names beside their amber points, and the caption TOKENS THAT ARE FOLLOWED BY THE SAME KIND OF TOKEN END UP NEAR EACH OTHER. No numbers, no axis labels, no other words. The amber cluster is the subject; keep it clearly apart from the black points. Each scene supplies the words it needs: the names of things, a short caption that states the lesson. Render exactly those words, in uppercase blocky glyphs, and invent no others. Never invent numbers or model output; a value appears only if the scene supplies it from a run.
